codebook_title: Existential Analysis and Logotherapy 4 Fundamental Motivations (EA LT 4FMs) Codebook
description: A comprehensive, merged codebook combining the best structural elements, detailed sub-themes, and specific psychopathology correlations from versions 1.3.2, 2.0, and 3.4, based on the four fundamental themes of existence (4FMs) in Existential Analysis and Logotherapy.

source_documents_list.apa_citation: Längle, A. (1992). What Are We Looking for When We Search for Meaning?. Ultimate Reality and Meaning, 15(4), 306–322. https://doi.org/10.3138/uram.15.4.306
source_documents_list.summary: Introduces the noetic (spiritual/existential) dimensions and the sequence of the three noetic motivations (True, Attractive, Right) leading to the will to meaning/act and a final transcendent commitment.

source_documents_list.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc.
source_documents_list.summary: Provides detailed breakdowns of the four types of coping reactions (psychodynamics) and failure results for each of the four fundamental motivations.

source_documents_list.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36.
source_documents_list.summary: Details the core existential motivations, their corresponding fundamental questions, core concepts, and the objective (goal of dialogue) of successfully dealing with each motivation.

source_documents_list.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers.
source_documents_list.summary: Defines the four fundamental themes/conditions of existence (4FMs) as the cornerstones of existence that challenge a person to respond and activate inner freedom.

general_concepts.definition: A process of **continuous exchange** between the subject individual and the environment, seen as a **dialogical movement** from the present, given reality towards the person's goals and intentions.
general_concepts.focus: An expression of the (mostly unconscious) human intention to **be-come**, to come into existence.

An **interpersonal paradigm** (a complement and counterweight to the individualistic paradigm of freedom and personal will). The most original activity of personhood: Our being essentially **dialogical**, prone to and directed towards **exchange with others**.
general_concepts.structure_function: The four cornerstones of existence form a **matrix for the psychopathological understanding** of psychological disorders and represent the **structural model for modern Existential Analytical Psychotherapy**.

general_concepts.längle_critique: In the motivational angle of his theory, Frankl may have adopted some **individualistic thinking** by tracing back and reducing the concept of existential motivation to the concept of **will**.

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: First Fundamental Motivation: The World—Dealing with Conditions and Possibilities
thematic_domains_4FMs.theme_name: The ability to be; to endure/uphold. (FM of World/Reality)
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_task: Coming to terms with the reality of one's existence, or 'being in the world'.
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome: Fundamental Trust, Confidence in Self, Faith
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_psychopathology: Phobic and anxiety disorders (in the extreme of this failure)

coping_reactions_failure.freezing_paralysis: Denial or Pretending to be Non-Existent

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: Second Fundamental Motivation: Life—Dealing with Relationships and Emotions
thematic_domains_4FMs.theme_name: The ability to feel value/life. (FM of Life/Value)
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_task: Coming to terms with the reality of one's life.
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_question: I am alive - do I like this fact? Is it good to be there?
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need: Value, Feeling, Value-Relation, Relationship, Time, and Closeness
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome: Fundamental Value, Harmony, Sense of Depth of Life
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_psychopathology: Depression (affective disorder, mood disorder) (in the extreme)

coping_reactions_failure.specific_aggression: Fury or Rage (to obtain or improve relationship)

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: Third Fundamental Motivation: Being a Person—Dealing with Uniqueness and Conscience
thematic_domains_4FMs.theme_name: The ability to be oneself; to be just. (FM of Self/Justice)
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_task: Coming to terms with an awareness of one's identity.
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_question: I am myself - may I be like this?
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_result_general: Solitude, Hysteria, Need to Hide behind Shame, Loneliness
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_psychopathology: Histrionic or borderline personality disorders (in the extreme)

coping_reactions_failure.freezing_paralysis: Dissociation (of bodily integrity), Dividing and Splitting (of emotion and cognition)

thematic_domains_4FMs.name: Fourth Fundamental Motivation: Meaning—Dealing with Becoming, Future and Commitment
thematic_domains_4FMs.theme_name: The ability to do good; to be creative/meaning. (FM of Meaning/Future)
thematic_domains_4FMs.core_task: To participate and be open to relationships and wider contexts (horizon) from which personal meanings are discovered.
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_question: I am there - for what is it good?
thematic_domains_4FMs.noetic_motivation: Will to act / Will to meaning
thematic_domains_4FMs.definition_of_existential_meaning: The Most Valuable, Realistic Possibility in the Given Situation, for which I feel I should decide myself.
thematic_domains_4FMs.existential_need: Meaning, Goal, Purpose, Future, A Field of Activity, A Structural Context, A Value to be Realized in the Future
thematic_domains_4FMs.positive_outcome: Sense of Fulfillment, Dedication, Action, Religious Belief
thematic_domains_4FMs.negative_pathology_result_general: Feeling of Emptiness, Frustration, Despair, Addiction, Absurdity
thematic_domains_4FMs.exclusion_criteria_psychopathology: Addictions, loss of identity (psychosis), and suicidal intentions (in the extreme of this failure)

coping_reactions_failure.freezing_paralysis: Fatalism, Loss of Interest, Apathy, Nihilism

transcendent_layer.name: Transcendent Meaning (Will to final commitment)
transcendent_layer.justification_quote: The seeker of meaning will then have to decide whether his search demands action and personal involvement (existential meaning) or refers to a 'meaning beyond' (Frankl) and the metaphysical transcendence.
